typography.usage: Native Title and research section headings use Baskerville.
Native Normal paragraphs use Baskerville 12 pt for the report narrative.
Subtitle, Caption, CaseMetadata and CaseEvidence use Gill Sans for supporting information.

recognitionRules: Use Baskerville for report headings and narrative paragraphs; use Gill Sans for subtitle, metadata, captions and evidence labels.
Keep study and task near the opening before findings.
Separate participant observations from the researcher’s interpretation.
Use dark green-gray table headers with white labels and pale rows; source IDs remain explicit in the black reading text.

principles: Move from observation to interpretation to a bounded next question.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Understand the task before judging the interface.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid “proves” when the material only supports a hypothesis.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: A record suggests a direction; it does not speak for every person.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE SERVICE STUDY in Gill Sans with a small report number and a thin rule. No magnifying-glass or person silhouette.
invariants: Use Baskerville for report headings and narrative paragraphs; use Gill Sans for subtitle, metadata, captions and evidence labels.
Keep study and task near the opening before findings.
Separate participant observations from the researcher’s interpretation.
adaptations: A short report retains method and limits even when findings are condensed.
An appendix expands the record without interrupting the main argument.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.
